To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the molecular hydrogen emission in some Seyfert galaxies is extended on kiloparsec scales, and that the morphology is related to the density of the surrounding media.

we have detected molecular hydrogen emission in the extended narrow line regions of six Seyfert galaxies, and that this emission is coincident with regions of high dust extinction and/or local star formation.

molecular hydrogen emission is observed on scales of 100 pc or larger in Seyfert 2 galaxies, but not in Seyfert1 galaxies, and that the morphology, excitation, and extinction of molecular hydrogen emission is different in different galaxies, suggesting that different processes are responsible for the molecular gas excitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interstellar medium in Seyfert 2 galaxies.
the physical conditions and the excitation mechanisms of the extended molecular gas near active galactic nuclei (AGNs).
the physical processes that are responsible for the excitation of molecular gas in the narrow-line regions of Seyfert galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
molecular hydrogen emission is associated with the narrow-line region, but the excitation mechanism depends on the density of molecular gas.
molecular hydrogen emission is a ubiquitous phenomenon in the narrow-line regions of active galaxies and that the emission can be excited by a number of mechanisms.
molecular hydrogen emission is a tracer of shocks, but it is unclear what causes the shocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the morphology and kinematics of molecular hydrogen line emission are determined by the ambient media and by the local excitation processes.

the molecular hydrogen emission in the Seyfert galaxies is from three distinct mechanisms: (1) shock excitation in the extended narrow emission-line regions, (2) UV fluorescence in the nuclear regions of Seyfert 2 galaxies, and (3) local star formation in Seyfert 3 galaxies.
molecular hydrogen emission is found near dust lanes in Seyfert 2 galaxies and near star formation sites in Seyfert and LINER galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the excitation of H2 in the extended narrow line regions of Seyfert galaxies is not a simple process.

there are multiple excitation mechanisms for molecular hydrogen in Seyfert nuclei and that there is a strong connection between the excitation mechanism and the morphology of the molecular hydrogen emission.
the morphology of molecular hydrogen emission is dependent on its local environment, and that the excitation mechanisms are likely to be different for different environments.
